partial_progress.details: Phase Mission restricted this dispatch to Phase 3 only (5-phase plan). Phase 3 completed and committed; phases 4-5 remain for subsequent dispatches.

artifacts.summary: Phase 3 completion handoff: sapience-retrieve.sh now sources lib/sapience-api-lib.sh, resolves the Phase 1 project binding, appends project_cid on success, benignly degrades on project_rejected, and the header contract is updated; next dispatch starts Phase 4.

completion_data.completion_summary: sapience-retrieve.sh now resolves a committed .sapience/project.json binding via lib/sapience-api-lib.sh's sapience_project_link_cid and appends &project_cid=<cid> to its /v1/search request when a valid binding resolves, appending nothing on any failure path (no-link byte-identity preserved). A 2xx response carrying a non-empty project_rejected prints one bounded stderr warning and falls through to the existing hit-extraction path on the same response, never exiting 2 or re-issuing the request. Four new link-present/malformed/project_rejected/non-2xx cases (19-22, 13 assertions) were added to test-sapience-capture.sh, and Phase 2's negative-control case 18 re-runs unmodified and still passes. All 59 assertions in test-sapience-capture.sh pass, test-sapience-context-scoping.sh's 6 cases pass, and a grep confirms project_cid appears nowhere in sapience-remember.sh or postflight-sapience-notes.sh outside the pre-existing Non-Goal header text.

sapience_notes.subject: project_cid placement inside sapience-retrieve.sh's response-handling pipeline
sapience_notes.value: The project_rejected benign-degrade check must sit AFTER the non-JSON-body guard and BEFORE the hit-list normalization step, reading the same already-parsed $response variable -- this lets the degrade path fall through to the existing hit-extraction code with zero duplication and guarantees no second network request is ever issued for this case.

sapience_notes.subject: project_cid vs project vs &project= on this vault's /v1/search endpoint
sapience_notes.value: This vault's /v1/search endpoint now has THREE distinct, non-interchangeable project-shaped identifiers in play: the plain &project= query parameter (confirmed dead -- silently ignored), the write-side's plain project (key) field sapience-remember.sh sends on /ingest-kos (unrelated endpoint, unrelated field), and the new project_cid query parameter sapience-retrieve.sh now sends on /v1/search, honored only when REPO_LINK_FOR is enabled for the account. Conflating any two of these three is an easy mistake when extending this extension's scripts.

sapience_notes.subject: deploy-headless.sh cleanly resolves gate3 deployed-script drift mid-task
sapience_notes.value: Running 'timeout 540 bash .claude/scripts/deploy-headless.sh' against a repo whose deployed .claude/ tree had drifted from the sapience extension's source store (5 files, from uncommitted Phase 1-2 edits) produced RESULT=landed_verify_clean and cleared all 5 gate3 deployed-script-content-drift FINDINGs on the next verify-touched.sh run, with zero hand-patching of .claude/** -- confirming the <deploy-freshness-context> remedy works cleanly as a mid-task corrective step, not only at session start.

sapience_notes.subject: a plan phase's own Tier Justification dependent-suite list disambiguates batch noise from real regressions
sapience_notes.value: Running verify-touched.sh under a heavy concurrent multi-task /orchestrate batch surfaced 2 FAILs (test-orchestrate-cycle-plan.sh, test-verify-deploy-gate-selection.sh) that named neither this phase's touched files nor any suite in this phase's own plan-authored Tier Justification dependent-suite enumeration. Checking that all 8 of the Tier Justification's own named suites passed gave a concrete, phase-scoped way to attribute the 2 unrelated FAILs to shared-working-tree batch noise from other concurrently-dispatched tasks rather than this phase's own edits, without needing to inspect those suites' internals.

sapience_notes.subject: test-verify-deploy-gate-selection.sh case(q) is a load-sensitive timing flake
sapience_notes.value: case(q) in test-verify-deploy-gate-selection.sh asserts VERIFY_DEPLOY_NESTED=1 is slower than an unguarded --jobs 4 run as proof the nested guard forces sequential execution; under a heavy concurrent multi-task /orchestrate batch it failed with the nested-guard run (19323ms) measuring FASTER than the unguarded run (22153ms) -- a second, distinct example (alongside the previously-recorded Gate 8 contention finding) of a wall-clock-comparison assertion in this test suite being unreliable under machine load, not a logic regression.
